content:
Sean Gallagher: Post-incident follow-up thread for yesterday’s regional capacity dip + retry storm (see incident channel links). Goal here: tie learnings -> hot-route capacity protection backlog + owners/dates. Please add corrections.

Sean Gallagher: tl;dr
- Enterprise lane helped for a couple routes but we still saw p99 blowups when router queues backed up.
- Biggest surprises: config propagation lag + inconsistent throttling semantics between gateway vs router.
- Retry behavior amplified load; we need clearer 429 + Retry-After + doc guidance.

IncidentBot: :memo: Incident summary snapshot
- Window: ~27m elevated latency/errors in us-east
- Symptoms: increased queue depth, elevated 5xx + client retries, partial GPU fleet degradation
- Impact: Hosted self-serve degraded; a subset of enterprise endpoints saw tail latency regressions
- Links: dashboards (lane health, router queue depth, throttled_count), runbook draft, timeline doc

Rafael Mendes: +1. For clarity: enterprise lane wasn’t fully rolled out to all top routes yet; the ones behind the flag behaved mostly as expected. The ones not flagged fell back to “best effort” and got crushed when retries started.

Talia Benson: thanks. I’ll translate the action items into Linear updates (ENG-4821 umbrella) once we agree on owners + dates.

Mina Haddad: On routing: we’re currently admitting too much into the enterprise lane when backpressure signals are noisy. Queue depth signal lags during prefill spikes -> we let the lane fill then everything stalls. We need earlier shed based on prefill saturation + a hard cap on in-flight per lane.

Sofia Ivanova: Agree. GPU util wasn’t the right trigger here; it stayed “fine” while prefill was saturated and decode got starved. We can provide a more stable “prefill_saturation” + “scheduler_backlog_ms” at 1s granularity, but we need to be careful w/ sampling overhead.

Allison Grant: Observability note: we also had a cardinality footgun. Someone flipped on per-tenant labels in a debug metric and it spiked TSDB load during the incident. We should add guardrails in the metrics lib + update the standard.

Amara Diallo: Gateway side: we returned 429 for rate-limit exceed, but router sometimes returned 503 for lane overload. Clients treat those differently; some retried aggressively on 503. We need to standardize (prefer 429 w/ reason codes) and ensure Retry-After is present.

Cole Summers: Quota enforcement: metering delay meant some tenants were effectively “unlimited” for ~10-15m. That’s expected in current design (fail-open on metering lag), but we should tighten the circuit: if metering lag > threshold, clamp to a conservative per-route RPS rather than unlimited.

Aisha Bello: Re dashboards: we didn’t have a single place to answer “are we protecting enterprise hot routes right now?” On-call bounced between router queue panels + gateway 429 panels + GPU dashboards. Suggest a consolidated "lane health" board + an incident mode view.

Sergio Costa: I can take the dashboard consolidation. Also: alerts fired too late because they were keyed on 5xx, not on queue depth + throttling spikes. Burn-rate alerts per route/tier will catch earlier.

Dev Patel: Support angle: we got 3 tickets in parallel asking “why 429 in us-east but not us-west” + “should we retry?” We need a crisp support macro w/ explanation + recommended exponential backoff + honoring Retry-After. Also need a comms snippet we can send proactively to top accounts.

Liam O'Rourke: For enterprise comms: if we’re going to say “priority lanes protect you,” we need to be clear what that means during partial region loss. Some customers interpret as guaranteed throughput. We should align language with Lauren/Nikhil but at least we can say: protected from noisy neighbors; still subject to regional capacity constraints; use multi-region + backoff.

Sean Gallagher: Action items draft (please react/confirm owners).

Sean Gallagher: 1) Standardize overload semantics across gateway + router
- Outcome: when shedding due to overload or lane admission control -> 429 + Retry-After + request id + reason_code.
- Owner: Amara (gateway) + Mina (router)
- Tracking: ENG-4826
- Due: end of next sprint

Sean Gallagher: 2) Backpressure signals: add prefill saturation + scheduler backlog; update admission thresholds
- Outcome: enterprise lane sheds earlier; cap in-flight; reduce tail latency under prefill spikes.
- Owner: Sofia + Mina
- Tracking: ENG-4825
- Due: prototype in 2 weeks, prod gated by canary

Sean Gallagher: 3) Config propagation + consistency checks
- Outcome: policy config changes propagate <60s p99; routers/gateways expose “config version” in metrics/logs.
- Owner: Benji (rollout) + Ethan/Jordan folks (cc later)
- Tracking: ENG-4828 (plus subtask)
- Due: initial version this month

Sean Gallagher: 4) Quota fail-open guardrail when metering lag is high
- Outcome: if metering lag > X, clamp to conservative per-route limit (still fail-open for enterprise allowlist).
- Owner: Cole
- Tracking: ENG-4823
- Due: spec by next Wed; implementation next sprint

Sean Gallagher: 5) Observability cleanup + consolidated dashboards + earlier alerts
- Outcome: Lane health dashboard; alert on queue depth + throttling spikes + config staleness; remove per-tenant label footguns.
- Owner: Sergio + Aisha + Allison
- Tracking: ENG-4827
- Due: dashboard this week; alert tuning after load tests

Sean Gallagher: 6) Client retry guidance + support macros
- Outcome: docs snippet + support response template; clarify 429 semantics + Retry-After; guidance for multi-region.
- Owner: Dev + Liam (loop in Nikhil/Lauren async)
- Tracking: PM-611 (and support ticket follow-up)
- Due: draft by Friday

Rafael Mendes: :thumbsup: on all. Minor tweak: for #3, we should explicitly add a runbook step: "check config_version parity" and a page when staleness >5m. That would’ve saved us.

Allison Grant: +1. For #5, I also want a hard rule in the metrics SDK: reject labels matching /tenant|customer_id/ unless explicitly allowlisted. We can enforce at CI for the observability-pack too.

Mina Haddad: For #2: I’m ok owning router threshold changes. Sofia, can you confirm the signals + their expected ranges so we can avoid tuning blind?

Sofia Ivanova: Yep. I’ll post a short doc with definitions + recommended thresholds. Also note: backlog_ms is per model group, so router needs to map request route->model group (it already does). Sampling at 1s is fine.

Amara Diallo: For #1: we can make gateway return the canonical error payload and have router reuse it (shared lib). Need to ensure SDK compatibility (pr-18463 touches this). I’ll sync with Cole since quotas share the same error envelope.

Cole Summers: 👍. Also: quotas will need to set reason_code distinct from rate_limit (e.g., QUOTA_EXCEEDED vs RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED vs OVER_CAPACITY). That’s part of ENG-4826 but just calling it out.

Sergio Costa: I’ll start the consolidated dashboard today. Aisha, can you list the “must-have” panels for on-call?

Aisha Bello: Must-have: throttled_count by tier/route, router queue depth per lane, lane utilization %, config_version/staleness, p95/p99 latency by tier for top 10 routes, and a "top reason_code" breakdown. Also link to runbook + feature flag state.

Dev Patel: I’ll draft the support macro and share in #support for review. Need exact wording for "retry after" guidance (max retries, jitter, etc). If anyone has strong prefs, reply here.

Liam O'Rourke: For enterprise comms, prefer: “honor Retry-After, exponential backoff with jitter, cap retries, avoid immediate retry storms.” Also call out that 429 is expected under protection and is not a billing error.

Talia Benson: Cool. I’ll update ENG-4821 with these as explicit deliverables + dates, and drop links here once done.

Sean Gallagher: last thing: we should schedule a mini-gameday focused on retry storms once #1/#2 are in canary. Rafael can you coordinate w/ Connor?

Rafael Mendes: yep, will coordinate. We’ll do a controlled load test in staging + a perf-canary run before prod. I’ll open a calendar hold.

Sean Gallagher: Thanks all. Please keep this thread updated as items move; we’ll review status in next reliability sync.
